artifact.summary: Qiskit phase-estimation operation for Shor order finding: H on t control qubits, controlled multiplication by a^(2^j) mod N on the work register (synthesized as cycles of basis-state transpositions using multi-controlled X gates), then inverse QFTGate on the control register. Input state (work=|1>, control=|0>) and measurement are left to the runner. Classical post-processing is not part of the circuit.
register_layout: qubits 0..t-1: control register, little-endian (qubit j has weight 2^j in y); controls controlled-U^(2^j)
qubits t..t+n-1: work register, n=ceil(log2 N), little-endian; work bit 0 is qubit t; runner should prepare |1> (qubit t set to 1)
example N=21,a=4,t=6: control qubits 0-5, work qubits 6-10 (11 qubits total)
control output after inverse QFT encodes y with y/2^t ≈ s/r

equation_mapping.explanation: Order definition is the property the circuit's eigenphases encode; r is not computed in the circuit, and the code only requires gcd(a,N)=1.
Classical gcd post-processing of even orders; not part of the circuit operation.

equation_mapping.code_location: build_circuit: H layer, controlled-U^(2^j) loop via _controlled_mult, QFTGate(t).inverse() on control qubits
equation_mapping.explanation: Phase-estimation circuit whose measured control outcome has distribution P(y). Measurement and continued fractions are left to the runner and post-processing.
Classical odd-order gcd rule for square a using b^r; no quantum content.
Classical relation between orders of a and sqrt(a); the paper's procedure is not specified.

specification_changes.change: The circuit contains only the phase-estimation operation (H on controls, controlled modular multiplications, inverse QFT). Work-register |1> preparation, measurement, and continued fractions are excluded.
specification_changes.reason: Task requires an operation without state prep or measurement; the runner prepares inputs.

specification_changes.change: The U_a black box is synthesized with standard gates: the permutation x -> m x mod N is split into cycles, then transpositions realized by CX conjugation and a multi-controlled X, instead of an opaque oracle. It acts as the identity on x >= N.
specification_changes.reason: Opaque dense unitaries are forbidden; this keeps the construction explicit and unitary.

specification_changes.change: Control-register size t defaults to min(2n, 12-n) and is user-selectable, so for N=21 it is at most 7 rather than about 2n.
The inverse QFT is QFTGate(t).inverse() on qubits 0..t-1, with no manual index reordering.
specification_changes.reason: Little-endian control encoding y=sum c_i 2^i makes QFTGate's bit-reversal convention match directly; no factorized-QFT index conflict arises.

specification_changes.change: Scope is narrowed to the quantum order-finding circuit for any valid (N,a,t); odd-order/square-coprime classical rules and relation combining are not implemented.
specification_changes.reason: They are classical post-processing and the paper's exact technique is not given.

assumptions: N>=3, 1<a<N, gcd(a,N)=1; n=ceil(log2 N) work qubits and t+n<=12.
The runner prepares the work register in |1> (qubit t = 1) and the controls in |0>.
Controlled U^(2^j) uses multiplier a^(2^j) mod N, skipped when it equals 1.
N need not be the product of two primes for the circuit itself.
unresolved_issues: Gate count grows with the number of cycles and may be large for larger N (still within the 12-qubit cap).
The paper's two-run relation-combining technique is not reconstructed.

validation.detail: Circuit built and transpiled successfully; no independent correctness reference selected.
